What is DHCP address pool (scope) exhaustion?
All available addresses in the DHCP scope have been leased
The DHCP server is powered off
What is the symptom of scope exhaustion for new clients?
New devices cannot obtain an IP address
A guest network keeps running out of addresses during busy events. What is the BEST fix?
Shorten the lease time or expand the scope
Which address does a Windows client self-assign when DHCP fails?
A host has a 169.254.x.x address while others have 10.x addresses. What is the likely cause?
The client couldn't reach the DHCP server or the scope is exhausted
Which practice helps resolve recurring scope exhaustion?
Right-sizing the scope and lease time for the number of devices
Which attack can intentionally exhaust a DHCP scope?
Which control helps prevent malicious DHCP scope exhaustion?
A /24 scope serves a network that grew to 300 devices. What is the problem?
The scope is too small for the number of devices
Which change expands addressing capacity for a growing subnet?
Using a larger subnet (e.g., /23) with a bigger scope
Which practice helps monitor for approaching scope exhaustion?
Tracking DHCP utilization and alerting on high usage
A lease time of 8 days on a high-turnover guest network causes exhaustion. What is the fix?
Reduce the lease time to recycle addresses faster
Which tool shows current DHCP leases to diagnose exhaustion?
A network adds many IoT devices and runs out of addresses. What is the BEST long-term fix?
Segment IoT into its own subnet with an appropriately sized scope
Which symptom indicates clients are failing to renew due to exhaustion or server issues?
Clients falling back to APIPA when leases expire
Which practice helps avoid exhaustion from stale leases?
Setting appropriate lease times so addresses return to the pool
A DHCP scope has many reservations and few dynamic addresses, causing exhaustion. What is the fix?
Review reservations and expand the dynamic range
Which practice helps diagnose whether exhaustion or connectivity is the cause of DHCP failure?
Checking scope utilization and client-to-server reachability
A rogue process requests many addresses, exhausting the scope. What control helps?
Which addressing approach reduces exhaustion risk for large flat networks?
Dividing into multiple subnets with separate scopes
A DHCP relay forwards requests, but a remote scope is exhausted. Where is the fix applied?
On the DHCP server's scope for that subnet
Which practice helps plan scope sizing?
Estimating peak concurrent devices plus growth headroom
Which symptom distinguishes scope exhaustion from a server outage?
The server responds but reports no available addresses
The server doesn't respond at all
A lease time set to a few minutes causes excessive DHCP traffic. What is the trade-off?
Very short leases recycle addresses but increase DHCP load
Which practice helps avoid conflicts while expanding a scope?
Ensuring new ranges don't overlap statics or other scopes
A network experiences exhaustion only during a seasonal event. What is a flexible fix?
Temporarily shorten leases or expand the scope for the event
Which tool or feature helps reclaim unused addresses?
Lease expiration and periodic cleanup of stale leases
Which addressing feature ensures critical devices always have addresses despite exhaustion?
A subnet needs 500 hosts. Which scope size is appropriate?
Which monitoring metric warns of impending exhaustion?
Which practice helps after resolving exhaustion?
Verifying new clients can obtain addresses
A guest with a short lease roams and reconnects frequently, consuming addresses. What helps?
Appropriate lease times and scope sizing for turnover
Which practice helps prevent exhaustion from unauthorized devices?
Network access control to limit who gets addresses
A DHCP server has multiple scopes; one is exhausted. What should be checked?
The utilization of each scope and whether the right scope serves the subnet
Which symptom suggests a specific VLAN's scope is exhausted while others work?
Only clients in that VLAN fail to get addresses
Which practice helps size leases for a mix of permanent and transient devices?
Using longer leases for stable devices and shorter for transient ones
A split-scope design helps with redundancy. Does it also affect capacity?
It divides addresses between servers, so total capacity should still meet demand
Which practice helps detect a DHCP starvation attack causing exhaustion?
Monitoring for abnormal DHCP request rates and many MACs on a port
Which addressing change reduces exhaustion for a doubling user base?
Expanding to a larger subnet and scope
A network uses IPv6 SLAAC and never exhausts addresses. Why?
IPv6's large address space provides ample addresses per subnet
Which practice helps document scope changes?
Recording scope ranges, lease times, and reservations in IPAM
Which symptom helps confirm exhaustion rather than a relay problem?
The server logs show the scope is full
Which practice helps avoid exhaustion when onboarding many devices at once?
Pre-planning scope capacity for the onboarding event
A device fails to get an address, and the scope shows 100% used. What is the cause?
Which fix increases available addresses without changing the subnet immediately?
Reducing lease times to recycle addresses faster
Which practice helps balance address availability and stability?
Choosing lease times appropriate to device turnover
A network admin excludes static addresses from the scope. How does this affect capacity?
It reduces the dynamic pool, so the scope must still be large enough
Which monitoring practice gives early warning before exhaustion causes outages?
Alerting when scope utilization crosses a threshold
Which addressing design BEST prevents future exhaustion for a campus?
Properly sized subnets per area with monitored scopes
Which BEST summarizes address pool exhaustion troubleshooting?
Recognize APIPA symptoms, check scope utilization, and resolve by adjusting lease times, expanding scopes, or controlling device access
